 Board directs Auditor-Controller’s Office to complete work by Oct. 27 
 EL CENTRO — The Imperial County Board of Supervisors directed the Auditor-Controller’s Office to complete work related to the county’s property tax levy and financial reporting by Oct. 27 following a discussion during its Tuesday, Oct. 20, meeting, according to a county press release.
 The discussion, presented by County Executive Officer Dr. Kathleen Lang, focused on the status of the fiscal year 2026-27 property tax levy and tax-roll process, as well as the county’s draft fiscal year 2024-25 audit and financial statements.
 According to the press release, the board reviewed the property tax levy process, which includes establishing tax rates for secured property throughout Imperial County, including rates associated with voter-approved school district and special district bonds.
 Supporting financial materials project approximately $178.6 million in gross revenue from secured property taxes and $24.1 million from unsecured property taxes for fiscal year 2026-27, according to the release. The figures represent countywide revenue projections and do not reflect funds exclusively available to the county’s General Fund.
 The board also reviewed the status of the county’s draft fiscal year 2024-25 audit and financial statements, which are part of its annual financial reporting and accountability responsibilities.
 Following the presentation, supervisors directed the Auditor-Controller’s Office to complete the necessary work related to the tax levy and financial reporting matters by Oct. 27 and return to the board for consideration and approval.
 The county said it remains committed to responsible financial management, timely reporting and transparency in the administration of public funds. Additional updates will be provided as the county continues to address the matters.
